text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are computer programs that understand and generate human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns learned from huge amounts of text, such as books, websites, and articles. This training data helps them answer questions, write texts, or translate languages. To get good results, users often use prompt engineering: writing clear and specific instructions. However, LLMs also have limits. They can make mistakes, give outdated information, or produce biased answers because they simply repeat patterns from their training data rather than truly understanding the world.
